newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU proposes anti-corruption aid clauses.
newsitem.headline: EU proposes anti-corruption aid clauses.

text.p: All European Union trade and aid accords with third countries should include an anti-corruption "good governance" clause, the European Commission said on Monday.

This would promote the "primacy of law, equity, transparency and integrity" in the public sector, European Development Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro said in a speech to parliamentarians from African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) countries.

"The fight against corruption is incontestably part of the priority actions that play a role in good governance," he added. He said the Commission would soon issue a proposal calling for the "good governance" clauses.
Deus Pinheiro noted that the EU and the ACP countries had since 1990 been including anti-corruption clauses in contracts for aid from the European Development Fund, but that more needed to be done.
He said the Commission also planned to intensify efforts to help beneficiaries of EU aid build independent judiciaries and implement appropriate laws and control mechanisms.
"This is not any more a matter of one field of cooperation, but of a new dimension in cooperation and partnership," he said.
Deus Pinheiro was speaking to a joint assembly of the European Parliament and deputies from the ACP countries.
